posts.title: Annenberg Lecture Speaker Offers Hope for a Better Information Economy
posts.dek: In this year's Annenberg lecture, Columbia professor Tim Wu offered hope amid shuttered newspapers, rising misinformation, disruptive AI, and concentrated media ownership.

posts.title: Missouri Educator’s Lesson Plan Chosen to Teach Video on Immune System
posts.dek: A high school lesson plan developed by a Missouri educator on how cells defend against foreign DNA has been chosen to teach about an animation by researchers at APPC and CHOP.

posts.title: Dolores Albarracín Receives Two NIH Awards to Advance AI-Powered Health Interventions
posts.dek: APPC director Dolores Albarracín received two NIH awards for research focused on using AI and community partnerships to address public health concerns.

posts.title: Public Knowledge That Alcohol Causes Cancer Rebounds
posts.dek: Nearly 6 in 10 Americans (58%) know that regularly consuming alcohol increases the chances of later developing cancer, a five-point increase from February 2026.

posts.title: One in 4 Americans Supports MAHA, but Three Times as Many Share Food-Related Concerns
posts.dek: An Annenberg survey finds that while just a quarter of Americans say they support the Make America Health Again movement, many more share its concerns over additives, chemicals, and highly processed foods.

posts.title: Views of Science Help Explain Partisan Differences Over Vaccine Safety and Effectiveness
posts.dek: How Americans view science and scientists is strongly associated with whether they think vaccines are safe and effective, according to a new study.

posts.title: Public Health Strategies Used Against Cigarettes Could Help Reduce Appeal of Firearms, Paper Argues
posts.dek: Dan Romer writes that public health strategies used to help reduce smoking offer an approach to help curb the appeal and use of firearms.

posts.title: About 1 in 3 Americans Say RFK Jr. Recommends Measles Vaccine
posts.dek: About a third of U.S. adults say HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. recommends vaccinating children against measles - and about as many say he does not recommend it.

posts.title: State HIV Prevention Policies May Benefit Racial and Ethnic Groups Unequally
posts.dek: State policies that make healthcare easier to obtain and protect LGBTQ+ people from discrimination are associated with greater use of HIV prevention measures among white adults. Those benefits may not extend equally to Black and Latino populations, a study finds.

posts.title: In House Primaries, Organized Groups Matter More Than Voters, New Book Finds
